rounds.fact: IGN started in 1996 focused purely on Nintendo 64 coverage before expanding into the general gaming and entertainment site it is today.
Tripod was a major free website-builder alongside GeoCities and Angelfire, and was eventually bought by Lycos as part of its portal strategy in the late 90s.
Monster.com ran one of the most memorable ad campaigns of the dot-com era ('When I grow up, I want to...') and became synonymous with online job searching in the late 90s.
Digital Trends grew as a general consumer-electronics review site during the mid-2000s, competing for readers alongside CNET and Engadget in a crowded gadget-blog era.
LiveJournal was one of the first blogging platforms to build in a real social layer, with friends lists and privacy settings, making it feel more like an early social network than a simple blog host.
